sentences.text:
Shri Mahendra Singh Rawat - Advocate for the appellant
 Shri Prabhat Pateriya - Dy. Public Prosecutor for resp
Heard on I.A. No. 4991 of 2024 which is first application under Section 389(1) Cr.P.C. for
suspension of sentence and grant of bail moved by appellants.

This Criminal Appeal assails the judgment dated 26.02.2024 passed in ST No.15/2022 by Sessions Judge Sheopur, District Sheopur (M.P.) whereby, appellants stood convicted under Section 363 of IPC and sentenced them to undergo four years RI with a fine of Rs.20,000/-, under Section 368 of the IPC and sentenced them to undergo four years RI with a fine of Rs.20,000/- with default stipulations.
Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the trial Court has wrongly convicted the appellants without proper appreciation of facts of the case.

It is further argued on the same set of evidence appellants have been acquitted from the charges of Sections 376(D), 376(2)(N), 506 Part-II of IPC and Sections 5G r/w. Section 6 & 5(L) of POCSO Act, however, due to previous statement of prosecutrix vide Exh.D/1 & D/2, the appellants have been convicted.
Further submission is that prosecutrix was minor at the time of incident is highly suspicious in the light of contradictions in respect to her date of birth.
In different documents, the statements of prosecutrix reveals that she left the house on her own volition, therefore, question of abduction does not arise.
The case is not supported by medical evidence.
The appellants have already served four and half months of incarceration out of total jail sentence awarded to them.
Present criminal appeal is likely to take long time to conclude.
Hence, prayed to suspend the jail sentence and grant of bail to appellants.
Counsel for the State vehemently opposed the application and prayed for its rejection.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the materials available on record.
Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, without commenting on merits of the case, I.A. No. 4991 of 2024 is hereby allowed.

Subject to depositing of fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing personal bond by each of the appellant in the sum of Ashok Suman vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59412752/
1 Rs.100,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only) each with a solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court, the remaining jail sentence of appellants shall remain suspended and they be released on bail.
